questions.question: The international date line is called ______.
questions.solution:
• **180° longitude** is known as the **International Date Line**.
 
• International Date Line is a fictitious line that demarcates the Earth’s surface.
 
• It runs from the North Pole to the South Pole and separates the transition of one calendar day to the next.
 
• IDL is located halfway around the world roughly at 180° longitude.

questions.question: Using Newton’s _____ ,we can measure force.
questions.solution:
• The Newton Second Law of Motion gives measurement of force.
 
• The Newton Second Law of Motion states that the rate of change of momentum of a body is directly proportional to the force applied on it and direction of the force applied.
 
• It can be stated as **F** **∝** **dp/dt** 
 
• where F is the force, dp is the rate of change of momentum and dt is the change in time.
 
• The above equation is further simplified to give F=ma
 
• Where F is the force, m is the mass of the body and a is the acceleration of the body.

questions.question: Which of the following doesn’t have kinetic energy?
questions.solution:
__CONCEPT__:

__
 
• Kinetic energy (KE): The energy possessed by a body by virtue of its motion is called kinetic energy.

KE = (1)/(2)m{v²}

Where m = mass of the body and v = velocity of the body

 
• Potential energy (PE): The energy possessed by a body by virtue of its position or configuration is called potential energy.

PE = mgh

Where, m = mass of the body, g = acceleration due to gravity, and h = height of the body

**EXPLANATION**__:

 
• **The stretched bow** doesn’t possess kinetic energy.
 
• It possesses **potential energy** as it is in a static position.
 
• Since** fired bullet, running water and working hammer are in motion,** they **possess kinetic energy**.
 
• Hence option 4 is correct.

questions.question: What is a mushroom?

__
 
• **Mushroom** is a **Fungi.**
 
• **Scientific Name:** **"Agaricus bisporus"** (Edible Mushroom).
 
• **Scientific Classification of Mushroom:**
 
 
• **Kingdom:** Fungi
 
• **Phylum:** Basidiomycota.
 
 
 
• Any of various fungi having a stalk topped by a **fleshy, often umbrella-shaped cap.**
 
• **Ecology of Mushrooms:**
 
 
• **Sporophores:** The** spore-producing organ** of a fungus or slime mold. **Two types of Sporophores are:**
 
 
• The term **Mushroom** is used to identify the **edible sporophores,**
 
• The term **Toadstool** is often reserved for** inedible or poisonous sporophores. **
 
 
 
• **​Parasites:** Parasites **grow on living trees and other plants, extracting their nutrients.**
 
 
• They are also called the** murderers among the mushrooms.**
 
 
 
• **​Mycorrhiza:** Mycorrhiza **forms a symbiotic association with the roots of living trees.**
 
 
• They take **sugars and nutrients from the tree**, but they **give back minerals and essential elements, enlarging the root system of their hosts.**
 
• **Like, **
 
 
• Porcini Mushrooms, 
 
• Chanterelles, and 
 
• Truffles.
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
• ​Mushrooms contain **no chlorophyll** which means **they can not photosynthesize.**
 
• Mushrooms are **a low-calorie source of fibre, protein, and antioxidants.**
 
• Mushrooms are a **good source of B vitamins.​**

questions.question: The outer cover of plant cell is called_____.
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__****Plant cell:**

__
 
• The outer cover of plant cell is called ‘**cell wall**’.
 
• It is a **structural layer** outside the cell membrane in the plant cells.
 
• It mainly provides **structural support and protection** to the plant cell and can **be tough, flexible** and **sometimes rigid**.
 
• **Tonoplast** is the layer of **vacuole** and **endoplasmic reticulum** is a **cell organelle**.

**Thus, the outer cover of the plant cell is called cell wall.**__
